records.quote: Example 1. Let (X1, X2, X3) ((X1*, X2*, X3*)) be a vector of independent heterogeneous GMW random variables. Set γ = 2, λ = 1.2, β = 0.5, (α1, α2, α3) = (0.1, 4, 6) and (α1*, α2*, α3*) = (0.1, 1, 8). Obviously (α1, α2, α3) ≼^w (α1*, α2*, α3*), and X3:3 and X3:3* are ordered in the reversed hazard rate order, as can be seen in Fig. 1. [Figure 1 caption, p. 107: Plot of the reversed hazard rate functions of X3:3 (black line) and X3:3* (red line).]
records.family: GMW(αi, γ, λ, β): F_i(x) = (1 − exp(−αi x^γ e^{λx}))^β; common γ = 2, λ = 1.2, β = 0.5

hypotheses.text: vector of independent heterogeneous GMW random variables
hypotheses.formal: Xi ∼ GMW(αi, 2, 1.2, 0.5), X*i ∼ GMW(αi*, 2, 1.2, 0.5), independent within each set

conclusion.direction: not printed in the text ('X3:3 and X3:3* are ordered in the reversed hazard rate order'); per Theorem 1, which this example illustrates, the direction would be X3:3 ≤rh X*3:3

records.numbers: γ = 2, λ = 1.2, β = 0.5; α = (0.1,4,6); α* = (0.1,1,8); evidence graphical only (Fig. 1), no function values printed
records.ambiguity: Direction of the rh order is not stated in the text — it is asserted graphically via Fig. 1 (X3:3 black, X*3:3 red). Printed relation '≼^w' is the paper's weak supermajorization (Definition 2(ii)).

note: Both passes agree: figure-supported rh comparison illustrating Theorem 1; direction not printed — Theorem 1 predicts X3:3 ≤rh X*3:3. Included with the unstated-direction caveat.

conclusion.direction: X1:3 ≥st X*1:3 as printed (i.e., X*1:3 ≤st X1:3)

records.quote: Theorem 10. Let X1, ..., Xn be a set of independent random variables with Xi ∼ GMW(α, γ, λi, β), i = 1, ..., n. Further, let X*1, ..., X*n be another set of independent random variables with X*i ∼ GMW(α, γ, λ*i, β), i = 1, ..., n. Then, for (λ1, ..., λn) ≼w (λ*1, ..., λ*n), we have X1:n ≥st X*1:n if β ≥ 1.
records.family: GMW(α, γ, λi, β): F_i(x) = (1 − exp(−αx^γ e^{λi x}))^β; α, γ, β common; λi heterogeneous

hypotheses.text: Xi ∼ GMW(α, γ, λi, β) and X*i ∼ GMW(α, γ, λ*i, β), independent within each set
hypotheses.formal: two series systems of independent GMW components differing only in λi
weak submajorization: Σ_{i=j}^n λ_(i) ≤ Σ_{i=j}^n λ*_(i), j = 1,...,n

conclusion.direction: X1:n ≥st X*1:n as printed (i.e., X*1:n ≤st X1:n)

records.ambiguity: Lead-in calls λ 'the scale parameter' while Section 1 calls α the scale parameter — notation inconsistency only. 'A_smaller'/'B_smaller' queue tags are the same printed direction.

note: Both passes agree on st under weak submajorization of λ with β ≥ 1; printed direction X1:n ≥st X*1:n.

records.quote: Theorem 15. For X ∼ ES(α, λ, ϕ1) and X* ∼ ES(α*, λ, ϕ2), (i) if ϕ1 or ϕ2 is log-convex, and ψ2 ◦ϕ1 is super-additive, then (α1, . . . , αn) ≽w (α1*, . . . , αn*) implies Xn:n ≥st Xn:n*;

hypotheses.formal: log ϕ1 convex or log ϕ2 convex
ψ2(ϕ1(x + y)) ≥ ψ2(ϕ1(x)) + ψ2(ϕ1(y)), where ψi = ϕi^{−1} is the pseudo-inverse
converse weak submajorization: α* ≼w α, i.e., Σ_{i=j}^n α*_(i) ≤ Σ_{i=j}^n α_(i) for all j

conclusion.direction: Xn:n ≥st X*n:n as printed (i.e., X*n:n ≤st Xn:n)

records.ambiguity: Quoted from Bashkar et al. (2018) — stated in the paper without proof as a numbered theorem. ES(α,λ,ϕ) notation: per eq. (10) the generator acts as the survival copula of X1:n; for parallel systems the paper's own Theorem 17 proof (eq. (12)) uses ϕ as the copula of the joint cdf — which convention applies here is not stated. '≽w' is the converse of Definition 2(i).

note: Both passes agree on st and direction. Stated as Theorem 15(i) in the paper (recited from Bashkar et al. 2018); included with the generator-role ambiguity noted.
